title: Reverse engineering of single-qubit quantum gates
authors: Gustavo Fernandes da Costa, Leonardo K. Castelano, Emanuel Fernandes de Lima
abstract: In this work, we address the problem of designing single-qubit quantum gates by means of a linearly-polarized field. We show that any desired one-qubit gate corresponding to a special unitary matrix can be generated by a modulated sinusoidal field. The only approximation involved is the rotating-wave-approximation. The formula for the control field is obtained by inverting the equation of motion for the evolution operator and imposing the conditions for the desired gate. We give a simple procedure to obtain closed analytical formulas for the fields in terms of a priori chosen dynamical functions. Additionally, these dynamical functions can depend on tunable free parameters intentionally introduced to meet a desired performance criteria.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous inverse engineering technique to determine the exact time-dependent electric field required to realize any desired single-qubit quantum gate. By solving the system's equations of motion and minimizing an associated cost functional, the authors provide optimal pulse shapes that ensure high fidelity while remaining analytically tractable.
main_problem: The core problem is designing the precise time-dependent control pulse required to implement an arbitrary single-qubit quantum gate using only a linearly-polarized external field.
main_result: The authors provide general closed analytical formulas for the control field, demonstrating that optimal pulses can be found by minimizing a cost functional (fluency) over free parameters derived from solving the system's equations of motion.
method: They employ an inverse engineering approach: deriving the required time-dependent Hamiltonian evolution operator and then inverting the resulting differential equations to determine the necessary field amplitude and phase functions.
model_or_system: The model is a two-level quantum system (qubit) governed by a Hamiltonian $H(t) = -\omega_0/2 \sigma_z - \mu E(t)\sigma_x$. The evolution is analyzed using the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA).
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($F$), control field amplitude $F(t)$, detuning $\Delta(t)$, and pulse fluency ($J$, a cost functional).
important_parameters: The initial/final state parameters of the target gate, such as $\phi_{ga}$ or $\delta^2$, which act as free parameters to optimize performance.
main_assumptions: The analysis fundamentally relies on the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA). Furthermore, achieving analytical tractability often requires assuming specific functional forms for intermediate dynamical functions.
figures_summary: Figures compare numerical simulations against derived analytical functions for implementing gates like $i\sigma_x$ and $i\sigma_z$, while Figure 5 maps the pulse fluency cost as a function of various free parameters to identify optimal control settings.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving general formulas for the control field using dynamical functions, then applies this framework to specific gates ($i\sigma_x$, $i\sigma_z$), and finally optimizes the resulting pulse parameters by minimizing a cost functional (fluency) via numerical comparison with full Hamiltonian simulations.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, analytically derived recipes for quantum control, which is crucial for experimental realization of quantum gates in platforms like trapped ions or superconducting qubits where precise microwave/laser pulses are used.
